Speed Skating starts here: every sound stopped (snd_jumps), both of CIA 1's ports set to input ($DC02 and $DC03 to 0), then, with interrupts off, a wait until the raster counter drops back to the top of a frame. Unlike the other events it keeps the menu's memory below $4C00 and the stack as they are.
CIA 1's interrupts off and any pending one acknowledged; then the variables at $10-$8F cleared (clear_vars) and $54-$55 pointed at $8800 for trail_fade, which nothing calls.
$01 = $25: the BASIC and KERNAL ROMs banked out and the I/O chips in, so the interrupt vector is the RAM at $FFFE, set here to ss_irq, with the first interrupt at line 251.

Where PLAY AGAIN comes back to: the screen built again (ss_screen), a dark grey background ($D021 = 11) and a black border, the sprites set up (setup_sprites), interrupts on, and the race set up for practice or competition (ss_start).
Code nothing reaches: it fills the page at $4000, the screen, with each byte's own offset and then stops in a loop on itself.

Skater X's speed class (speed_class) is its speed in half pixels a frame, the low four bits of it. Every frame stride_clocks gains 48 (sample_steps), and when it passes 256, about every 5.3 frames, the stride moves on: a finished skater goes to state 16, or 17 if it won; otherwise the stick, or the pacer's choice (pacer_stick), picks the next state from stride_none, stride_right or stride_left.
The joystick of skater X: port 2 or port 1, swapped by port_swap, so the skater whose button was pressed first is the bottom one.

The next stride state with the stick in neither direction, for states 0 to 9: a stroke at full stretch (2 and 7) eases back (3 and 8) and comes upright to glide (4 and 9), where it stays; let go during a push (0, 1, 5 or 6) and the stroke drops back to the glide it started from (9 or 4). Index 16, the standing skater, reads the first byte of stride_right: 1.

The next state with the stick right: from the glide in 9 the right stroke begins (0, 1, 2, held at 2); 3 goes on to 4, where right does nothing; right during the left stroke (5 to 8) cuts it short to 9. Index 16 reads stride_left's first byte, 4.

The next state with the stick left: from the glide in 4 the left stroke begins (5, 6, 7, held at 7); 8 goes on to 9, where left does nothing; left during the right stroke (0 to 3) cuts it short to 4. Index 16 reads push_states' first byte, 1.
stride_left's sixteenth byte, past the states it is read for.
Whether each state pushes: 0, 1, 5 and 6, the first two samples of each stroke. Speed is gained only in these.
The speed lost each frame, in 256ths of a pixel, by speed class: 5 below 3 pixels a frame, then 6, and from 4 pixels a frame 13, 21, 29 and so on up to 69.
What stride_clocks gains each frame, by speed class: 48 for every class.
The speed gained each frame of a push, by speed class: 48/256 of a pixel for every class.
The joystick's right bit ($08).
Its left bit ($04).
The two skaters' stride clocks.
The two skaters' push counts: a push starts at 6, and gains nothing for its first six frames.
Whether each skater's last state pushed.

A frame's push and friction. In a push state, the first frame of a push sets push_delays to 6 and it counts down, and from the seventh frame on each frame adds push_gains to the speed; outside a push the count is cleared. Then friction by the speed class, with the speed kept from going below 0.
Skater X's speed bar at column 29 of its status row, once it has moved (bar_on): the speed in quarter pixels a frame, up to 16.

Two bytes nothing reads.
Set by F5 and cleared by F3 (irq_keys). Nothing reads it.
A frame number for each skater from its place, its place over eight in steps of 0 to 14, or 15 standing, into $5A and $5B. set_frames adds 6 to the base it reads with them and throws the sum away.

Both skaters' frames: each skater's stride state picks the first of eight sprite blocks (frame_bases), which go to skater_frames and skater_frames_2, and the two x positions of its fixed place (far_top, near_bottom) from x_offsets_3 and x_offsets_4; then into the interrupt's immediates (set_near_top, set_near_bottom).

The first sprite block of each stride state's frame, eight blocks a frame: states 0 to 7 at $30-$6F ($4C00-$5BFF), 8 at $C0 and 9 at $C8 ($7000-$73FF), 16, standing, at $D0 and 17, the winner, at $D8 ($7400-$77FF).
For each stride state, sprite 3's x less $75: 16 for every state.
For each state, sprite 4's x less $75: 40 for every state.

The start: a wait until the frame count passes 60 (wait_frames with Y = 60, 61 frames), READY on both status rows with a beep (sound 9), the same wait, SET with another, the same again, GO with a burst of noise for the gun (sound 11), and the GO turned yellow.
Waits until the frame counter (frames), cleared here, passes Y.
Shows word Y (READY, SET or GO) on both status rows.
Writes word Y in white at column 29 of status row X, through the immediates of the loop below.
The low byte of the word's address in show_word_row, from word_lo.
The word's high byte, from word_hi.
The low byte of the status row's column 29, from word_rows_lo.
That column's high byte, from word_rows_hi.
The low byte of the column's colour RAM, the same as the screen's.
The colour RAM's high byte, the screen's plus $98.
The two status rows' column 29, low bytes: $41FD and $43DD.
Column 29's high bytes on the two status rows, $41 and $43.
The three words' addresses, low bytes.
The three words' high bytes, all $A2.
"   READY  ", ten characters.
"    SET   ".
"    GO    ".
The right stick for the pacer's stride state, from pacer_right.
For states 0 to 9, the stick a good skater holds, as the joystick port reads it (a 0 bit pressed): right in 9, 0 and 1, left in 4, 5 and 6, nothing in 2, 3, 7 and 8.
The pacer's other choice: the same but for 2 and 7, where it keeps the stroke's direction, so the stroke stays at full stretch.
Code nothing reaches: a return, then the top skater's place over eight, its low three bits.

The computer pacer's stick, in place of a joystick. Its skill (pacer_skill) is moved first (pacer_adjust). A random byte ($22, shifted and mixed each call) mixed with the frame count is compared with the skill: below it the pacer takes pacer_right, otherwise pacer_late.
The pacer's rubber band: while the player is ahead of it, or level, its skill goes up by one each call, to 255 at most; while it leads, down by one (two while it is above 160), to 56 at least.
"COMPUTER PACER  ".

Clears the result byte (+$10) of all eight players' records. In practice ($081D negative) the bottom skater is the player, the top one the computer pacer: one race (ss_race, with its replays), then the loader's entry at $0900 to load the menu again.

In a competition each player in turn ($21, from 1) races in the bottom lane. With two joysticks ($087D) the next player in the list races in the top lane, so players go in pairs; the last of an odd number, and every player with one joystick, races the pacer. After the last, back to the menu through $0900.

Into the player's record, $16-$18 then the time turned over, which the menu ranks highest first, so the fastest time ranks first: the seconds EORed with $FF, the tenths and the minutes EORed with $FF and kept to their low four bits; and $10-$15 the time as the status row shows it. In a pair the top player's record too; then the next player, or two on.
Waits for a fire button on either port, through no_wait; then the status rows cleared.

The far top skater blue and the near bottom skater red; then the bottom lane's PRESS YOUR BUTTON flashes, and its skater with it, until a button is pressed. Its port becomes the bottom lane's (port_swap), with a blip (sound 10). Against another player the top lane's prompt then flashes until the other port's button is pressed.
Writes " 0:00.0" and spaces over columns 18 to 38 of both status rows, in white.
" 0:00.0" and fourteen spaces, which clear_status writes; from its 21st byte "PRESS YOUR BUTTON   ", which the flashing prompts write.
"PRESS YOUR BUTTON   ", which flash_top and flash_bottom write at column 18.
After line 55, the fire buttons: 1 for port 2, 2 for port 1, 0 for none.
The top lane's prompt, in white, and its far skater in light blue, or yellow and blue, sixteen calls each.
The bottom lane's prompt and its near skater, white and light red or yellow and red.
Waits for raster line 55 to start.
Code nothing reaches: it would point $14-$15 at player X's record; then " PRESS YOUR BUTTON." and spaces that nothing prints.
" PRESS YOUR BUTTON." and spaces, which nothing prints.
The sound of a skate's push at the start of each stroke (stroke_sounds): for the bottom skater sound 5 or 6, on voice 1, for the top one 7 or 8, on voice 2.
The sound for each stride state of the bottom skater: 5 in state 1, 6 in state 6.
The top skater's: 7 in state 1, 8 in state 6.
194 bytes nothing reads, a repeating fill.
The engine's three entries: stop_all here, start_sound at $A603 and sound_step at $A606, which the event calls by these addresses.
start_sound's entry.
sound_step's entry, called once a frame from irq_keys.

Starts sound A (100 and above are ignored) from snd_table: its first byte is the slot it plays in, its second the SID voice; the slot's script starts at its third byte on the next frame, with its transposition, tuning and slide cleared. A sound already playing in that slot is cut off. X and Y are kept at $AEF1-$AEF2, and the engine is held off ($AE8C = 0) while the slot is written.
Code nothing reaches: it steps the slot pointer at $60-$61 by one.
Steps the script pointer at $62-$63.
Steps the pointer at $66-$67 through a sound's first bytes.

The sound engine's frame, while it is on ($AE8C). For each of the three slots that is not idle: the slide's step added to the frequency, every frame; the slot's count of frames taken down, and at zero the next step of its script (script_step). The other events' copies first test the S key; this one has no such test.
On to the next slot, 32 bytes on.

Copies the slots to the SID, slot 2 first and slot 0 last, so where two slots play one voice the lower-numbered wins: each slot that is not idle writes its seven registers to its voice (sid_voices), and a slot's restart flag turns the gate off and on again to restart the envelope, and is cleared. Then the filter's four bytes ($AE8D-$AE90) to $D415-$D418.
The SID's three voices' register addresses, $D400, $D407 and $D40E.
The voices' register addresses' high bytes, read one on from sid_voices.

Stops every sound: the engine held off, the slots and variables at $ADC8-$AEC7 cleared, volume 15 with the low-pass mode and nothing filtered, each slot idle with its stack pointer set from slot_stack_addrs, the SID's voice registers cleared (sid_clear), and the engine on again.
The slots' stack addresses, $AE91, $AEA1 and $AEB1, sixteen bytes each, then three more for slots this engine does not have.
Writes 0 to the SID's registers $D400-$D415.
The addresses of the event's 31 sounds, by number, for start_sound. Each is a slot, a SID voice and a script.
The sounds' addresses' high bytes, read one on from snd_table.
Sounds 1 to 4 and 12 to 28, which the event never starts: slot 0 on voice 2, and at once the stop command.
Sound 11, at GO: noise on voice 0 that dies away (attack 0, decay 9, no sustain), the filter's cutoff, routing and mode set to 0, one note for 64 frames, then stop.
Sound 10, as a fire button is pressed at the start: a triangle on voice 0 at full sustain, four times two notes of a frame each, A and the C below it in the top octave, then stop.
The blip's two notes, which the loop command repeats.
Sound 9, at READY and SET: a triangle note, the G in the top octave, for 8 frames.

Sounds 5 and 6, the bottom skater's push: noise on voice 1 for 32 frames, at the top of its range, through the band-pass filter (cutoff $38, full resonance, voices 1 and 2 filtered): the scrape of a skate.
Sounds 7 and 8, the top skater's push: the same on voice 2 with the cutoff at $48.

Sound 29, the music's bass on voice 0, which the tune starts: a sawtooth two semitones up, an A and the A an octave above in a bar of 112 frames (14, 7, 14, 14, 7, 7, 7, 14, 7, 7, 14), round and round.
Where the bass goes round again.

Sound 0, the music, while the game waits for the button before a race and after it: it starts the bass (sound 29) and the drums (sound 30), then plays the melody on voice 1, a pulse wave two semitones up. The melody waits 210 frames, then plays four bars, each four notes of 7 frames, A and E high up, and a low A held for 84; the third bar drops a tone halfway, and the fourth holds its last note for 98. The whole tune is six bars, 672 frames, and it plays until stop_all.
Where the melody goes round again, the rest first.

Sound 30, the drums and an answer to the melody on voice 2, two semitones up, through the band-pass filter: noise that falls fast in pitch (the slide's step -$1800 a frame from the top), seven beats of 28 frames; then, with the cutoff low, a pulse-wave answer to the melody's figure, E and A and a held A, which starts with each of the melody's bars; between them two beats; the third time it drops a tone halfway, with the melody; two last beats end the six bars.
Where the drums go round again.

Runs a slot's script from ($62) until it waits. A byte under $80 is a note: its pitch (set_note), then a byte of how many frames it lasts, and the gate on with the envelope restarted. From $80 a command, its number in the low seven bits, through snd_commands, with its first byte in A; numbers above 28 stop the sound (cmd_stop).
Steps past a command's last byte and runs the next.
An RTS that nothing reaches.
A note: its pitch, then its length (snd_length).
Steps past the length, then sets the restart flag and the gate on. The slot waits there until its count runs out.

The 29 commands' routines: 0 set the loop count, 1 loop to an address while the count lasts, 2 start another sound, 3 call machine code, 4 jump to an address, 5 call a part of a script, 6 return from it, 7 end, 8 stop, 9 transpose, 10 tune, 11 jump to machine code, 12 stop as 8 does (the other events' note with a pulse width), 13 a tied note (no new envelope), 14 the gate off for a time, 15 attack-decay and sustain-release, 16 the waveform and envelope, 17 the pulse width, pulse waveform and envelope, 18 a raw frequency for a time, 19 the slide off, 20 a sweep nothing performs, 21 the slide, 22 the volume, 23 the resonance, 24 the cutoff, 25 the filter mode, 26 the voices filtered, 27 cutoff, mode and resonance from three bytes, 28 cutoff, resonance and routing, and mode.
The command routines' high bytes, read one on from snd_commands.
Command 11: jumps to the machine code at its two bytes; its RTS ends the slot's step.
Command 3: calls the machine code at its two bytes, then goes on with the script.
Jumps through $64-$65.
Back from the machine code to the next command.
Command 7: the slot goes idle.
Command 8, 12, and any number above 28: the slot's registers and effects cleared, the gate left on with no waveform, and two frames later the end command at snd_end_byte.
Command 7 ($87), where cmd_stop points the script.

Sets the slot's frequency from a note byte: the high four bits the octave, the low four the semitone, plus the slot's transposition, from note_freqs shifted right once for each octave under 7; 15 gives the highest frequency, $FFFF, for noise. The slot's fine tuning is added.
The SID frequencies of 24 semitones from C in the top octave: C is $430F, which is 1046.5 Hz on an NTSC machine and two-thirds of a semitone flat on a PAL one, as in the other events' tables.
The frequencies' high bytes, read one on from note_freqs.
Code nothing reaches: a read, a step and a read.
Command 16: the control byte (waveform and gate), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 17: the pulse width, then the pulse waveform with the gate ($41), attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 18: a frequency of two bytes, then a length and the gate on.
A note's length, then the gate on.
Command 4: the script goes on at its two bytes.
Command 1: the loop count less one; until it reaches 0 the script goes back to its two bytes' address, then on past them.
Command 0: sets the loop count.
Command 2: starts another sound, the other voices of a tune.
Command 5: pushes the address after the command onto the slot's stack and goes to its two bytes' address.
Command 6: back to the address on the slot's stack.
Command 9: the slot's transposition, in semitones (kept doubled, as an offset into note_freqs).
Command 10: the slot's fine tuning, added to every frequency.
Command 22: the volume, the low four bits of $D418.
Command 24: the filter's cutoff, high byte.
Command 25: the filter mode, the high four bits of $D418.
Command 26: which voices go through the filter, the low four bits of $D417.
Command 23: the resonance, the high four bits of $D417.
Command 27: the cutoff from the first byte and the top bit of the second, the mode from the second's low four bits and the cutoff's low bits from its high four, then the resonance and routing.
Two bytes nothing reads, between the filter commands.
Command 28: the cutoff's high byte, the resonance and routing, and the mode.
Command 19: the slide stopped. It has no bytes of its own.
Command 21: a rate byte, which this engine keeps but never reads, and the slide's step of two bytes, added to the frequency every frame.
Command 20: a pulse-width sweep's period and step, which this engine keeps but never performs.
Code nothing reaches: a note command, pitch, length and gate.
Command 13: a new pitch and length with no new envelope, the notes tied.
Code nothing reaches: a pulse-width command.
Command 15: attack-decay and sustain-release.
Command 14: the gate off, and a wait of its byte's frames.

The file's last byte, and the first of the sound engine's three slots, 32 bytes each, which run on past the file: +0 the SID voice the slot plays on (0 to 2), bit 7 set when it is idle; +1-2 the script's address; +3 the frames until its next step; +4 a loop count; +5-6 its stack pointer; +8 to +14 its copy of the voice's seven registers; +15 a flag that restarts the envelope; +16 its transposition; +17 a fine tuning; +18-19 the slide's step; +21 the slide's rate and +22-24 a sweep, which nothing reads. After the slots: $AE88 the slot count of sound_step's loop, $AE8C nonzero while the engine runs, $AE8D-$AE90 the filter's registers, $AE91 the slots' stacks and $AEF1-$AEF2 start_sound's copies of X and Y. stop_all writes $80 over this byte.
Slot 0's script address (+1 and +2), the base start_sound writes each slot's through.
The script address's high byte, slot 0's +2.
Slot 0's count of frames to its next step (+3).
Slot 0's transposition, tuning, slide and sweep (+16 to +25), which start_sound clears for the slot it starts.
The third slot, and stop_all's second 64 bytes to clear.
stop_all's third 64 bytes to clear, after the slots.
The slot count of sound_step's loop.
Nonzero while the engine runs; start_sound clears it while it writes a slot.
The filter's registers, copied to $D415-$D418 every frame: the cutoff's low and high bytes, the resonance and the voices filtered, the filter mode and the volume.
The cutoff's high byte, for $D416.
The resonance and the voices filtered, for $D417.
The filter mode and the volume, for $D418.
The three slots' stacks for the scripts' calls, sixteen bytes each.
start_sound's copy of X.
start_sound's copy of Y.
